title: Pricing simplification launch sequencing & operational playbook
creator: Sofia Martínez
description: High-level playbook for launching the pricing and SKU simplification initiative. Covers sequencing, release notes coordination, billing migration steps, console UI updates, sales and support enablement, and rollback criteria. Goal is to reduce SKU complexity, consolidate overlapping tiers, and migrate existing customers with minimal billing disruption and clear messaging.
scope: Includes SKU consolidation, per-route limits migration, entitlement mappings, billing engine migration scripts, console product page updates, pricing table copy, API compatibility shim for deprecated parameters. Excludes deep rate-limiting rewrite or changes to dedicated capacity SLAs.
success_metrics: <1% API errors due to parameter changes during rollouts
Successful migration of 95% self-serve customers within 14 days of offer change
Sales and Support NPS change <= 0.5 points attributable to pricing confusion
milestones: 2026-03-10: Finalize SKU mapping matrix and entitlement table
2026-03-24: Console pricing page & API deprecation notice drafts ready
rollout_strategy: Phased rollout: internal -> opt-in beta -> region-limited soft launch -> global switch. Start with low-risk customers (no custom pricing) and stagger quotas and billing migration windows by cohort. Provide an automated opt-in migration for self-serve customers and a managed migration path for enterprise customers handled by CS/AM.
rollback_criteria: Significant billing reconciliation errors > 1% of migrated accounts, API regression producing >0.5% 4xx/5xx spikes, or widespread console UI regressions preventing checkout. If any criterion met, pause migration, revert billing engine flag, and activate rollback runbook within 2 hours.
billing_migration_steps: Generate SKU mapping CSV for each customer account
Dry-run migration to staging billing database and validate totals
Ship migration scripts with feature flag; run on a 1% sample in staging
Execute opt-in migration window for self-serve with email + console prompt
Coordinate managed migrations with CS for enterprise customers
Run reconciliation job and publish variance report to #billing-alerts channel
console_and_api_changes: UI: Update pricing tables and limits pages with new SKUs and contextual tooltips
API: Add compatibility shim for legacy sku_id parameter (deprecated) with 6-week grace
Docs: Add migration guide and example API calls
SDKs: Patch SDKs to map legacy fields client-side where feasible
release_notes_outline: What changes for customers: SKU names, limits, and pricing tiers
How billing will be affected and migration timeline
Known compatibility shims and deprecation windows
How to opt-in or request managed migration
Support contact flow and expected SLAs during migration
comms_templates:
Customer email (pre-launch): Subject: Upcoming changes to Redwood pricing — action recommended
Body: Brief rationale, migration timeline, opt-in button link, support contact

Customer email (launch): Subject: Your account has been migrated to simplified pricing
Body: Account-level summary, invoice impact, link to migration report
Sales enablement one-pager: Short FAQ + objection handling + migration playbook for AMs
Support canned responses: Billing dispute triage steps and escalation path
sales_enablement_tasks: Create one-pager and slide deck for AMs
Run two 60-minute enablement sessions and record for on-demand
Prepare customer-facing ROI examples and migration benefits
Update pricing calculator in sales playbook
Create list of top 50 enterprise customers requiring manual outreach
monitoring_and_postlaunch: Dashboards: billing variance by cohort, migration success rate, API error spike monitors
Weekly post-launch sync for first 4 weeks: PM+Eng+Billing+Support
Customer satisfaction sampling: targeted surveys 7 and 30 days post-migration
Automated alerting to #oncall-billing for reconciliation anomalies
